title: A common injective resolution for etale/proetale comparison
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $A$ a finite commutative ring. Use ordinary sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaves on the small etale and pro-etale sites, in a common larger universe in which both sites are small [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $
u_T^*\dashv
u_{T,*}$ be the comparison adjunction [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], and let $F$ be an etale $A$-module sheaf, viewed as a complex in degree zero. Put $F_p=
u_T^*F$ and denote the ordinary adjunction unit by $\eta_F^0:F	o
u_{T,*}F_p$.

There exists a bounded-below injective resolution $h:F_p	o J^ ullet$ in ordinary pro-etale $A$-module sheaves [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. For every such resolution, set $I^ ullet=
u_{T,*}J^ ullet$ and $a=
u_{T,*}(h)\circ\eta_F^0$. Then $a:F	o I^ ullet$ is a bounded-below injective resolution in ordinary etale $A$-module sheaves. Under the canonical injective computation $QI^ ullet\cong R
u_{T,*}F_p$ [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective], its augmentation $Qa$ is the derived adjunction unit $F	o R
u_{T,*}
u_T^*F$ of [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]. Here $Q$ is localization at quasi-isomorphisms.

For every etale object $W	o T$, direct-image evaluation gives $I^ ullet(W)=J^ ullet(W)$ as complexes of $A$-modules, compatibly with every etale-site restriction arrow and with the differentials. In particular, for any closed immersion $i:C\hookrightarrow T$ and complementary open immersion $j:V\hookrightarrow T$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion], there is the literal kernel identification
$$\ker(I^ ullet(T)	o I^ ullet(V))=\ker(J^ ullet(T)	o J^ ullet(V)),$$
with the same kernel inclusions and restriction arrows, using the support convention of [def-pur-support-cohomology]. No constructibility or freeness hypothesis is imposed on $F$.

proof.text: Work in the common larger universe specified in the statement. Apply the ringed-site Grothendieck theorem to each of the two small sites with its constant sheaf of rings $A$. Both ordinary module-sheaf categories are abelian and Grothendieck, hence have enough injectives. The degree-zero complex $F_p[0]$ is bounded below. The bounded-below resolution-existence theorem therefore supplies a quasi-isomorphism $h:F_p[0]\to J^\bullet$ with $J^\bullet$ bounded below and each $J^n$ injective. This proves the existence clause; fix any such $h$ for the remaining steps.

proof.text:
The comparison inverse image on the stated fixed-$A$ module categories is left adjoint to $
u_{T,*}$, and by the comparison-pullback exactness lemma (clause 2) it is additive and exact. Thus the right-adjoint preservation theorem applies to every injective $J^n$: $I^n=
u_{T,*}J^n$ is injective. Direct image is additive and sends zero objects to zero objects, so its termwise application gives a complex $I^ ullet$ with the same lower bound as $J^ ullet$. The composite $a=
u_{T,*}(h)\circ\eta_F^0$ is a chain map from $F[0]$. No assertion that direct image is exact is used.

source.place: Tag 09B1, lemma-compare-derived, proof: inverse image is exact; right-adjoint injectivity is the generic statement of lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives.

proof.text:
Write $R=R
u_{T,*}$ and let $\alpha_K:Q(
u_{T,*}K)	o R(QK)$ be the natural comparison of the cited injective computation theorem. Since $J^ ullet$ is bounded below with injective terms, $\alpha_J$ is invertible; since $h$ is a quasi-isomorphism, $R(Qh)$ is invertible. The canonical injective computation for this resolution is $	heta=R(Qh)^{-1}\circ\alpha_J:QI^ ullet\xrightarrow{\sim}R(F_p[0])$. Apply the comparison-unit injective-model lemma with $\Lambda=A$, the bounded-below complex $M=F[0]$ and $j=h:
u_T^*M=F_p[0]	o J^ ullet$; its hypotheses are exactly steps 1 and 2. Its displayed equation reads $R(Qh)\circ\eta^D_F=\alpha_J\circ Q(
u_{T,*}(h)\circ\eta_F^0)=\alpha_J\circ Qa$, where $\eta^D$ is the derived adjunction unit of the site-comparison theorem. Hence $	heta\circ Qa=\eta^D_F$. This pins down the augmentation, rather than choosing an arbitrary isomorphism to the derived image.

source.place: Tag 05TI, lemma-enough-injectives-right-derived, (2); the unit representative is the statement of lem-pur-comparison-unit-injective-model.

proof.text: The site-comparison theorem says that this derived unit is an isomorphism for every bounded-below etale module complex; apply it to $F[0]$. By step 3, $\theta\circ Qa$ is this unit; as $\theta$ is an isomorphism, $Qa$ is an isomorphism. The cohomology-sheaf functors on the derived category compute the cohomology of any representing complex, so $H^n(a)$ is an isomorphism for every $n$. Thus $a$ is a quasi-isomorphism, and together with step 2 this makes $a:F[0]\to I^\bullet$ a bounded-below injective resolution. The comparison theorem explicitly imposes no constructibility or finiteness on the individual sheaves.

By the explicit direct-image definition, for every etale $W\to T$ and every degree $n$ one has $I^n(W)=(\nu_{T,*}J^n)(W)=J^n(u_T(W))=J^n(W)$. An etale arrow $W_1\to W_2$ is sent by $u_T$ to the identical scheme arrow, so both restrictions are the same $J^n(W_2)\to J^n(W_1)$. Likewise the differential on $I^\bullet(W)$ is $d_J^n(W)$, since direct image acts on a sheaf morphism by its components at $u_T(W)$. Hence these are identical complexes, including all restriction arrows. In particular $T$ and its open $V$ are etale objects, and both maps in the support-kernel formula are the same map of complexes. Their degreewise kernels and kernel inclusions are therefore literally equal. This uses only the kernel-of-restriction convention for supported sections; no comparison of separately chosen kernel models or of derived support functors is needed.
